title: Subjunctive Concessive Clauses with Indefinite Pronouns
grammar: Concessive Subjunctive Structures in Civic Defiance
goal: I can form inverted subjunctive concessive clauses (*történjék bármi, hozzon a hatalom bármilyen rendeletet*).
I can deploy vocabulary of non-compliance and resistance (*passzív rezisztencia, megingathatatlan*).
I can express unconditional ethical defiance in formal C1 Hungarian.

sections.title: Unit 12: Civic Resistance, Dissent & Legal Philosophy
body: Hungarian discourse surrounding civic resistance, dissent, and legal philosophy bridges jurisprudence with moral philosophy, utilizing concessive subjunctive syntax (történjék bármi; döntsön bárhogy a hatalom), ethical stance adverbials (lelkiismereti meggyőződésből fakadóan), and the classic jurisprudence of supra-statutory law.

In this capstone unit of Block 2, anchored by György Konrád's landmark philosophical work 'Az autonómia kísértése' (Antipolitics / The Temptation of Autonomy, 1980), you will dissect the vocabulary and syntax of passive resistance, civil disobedience, and conscientious objection.
